justification: Cancel Premium dialog with clear Unsubscribe and Keep subscription buttons, all states identical; direct, honest opt-out.
Order summary shows Pro Plan $89.00, tax $7.12, and total due $96.12 with a cancel order link; all costs disclosed up front.
Gambling-style spin wheel with streak-loss urgency ('Daily bonus resets soon. Don't lose your streak!') and variable-ratio rewards; footer even admits 'dopamine on a schedule'.
Signup form with essential ToS checkbox and data-sharing checkbox explicitly labeled Optional with 'you can stay opted out'; honest.
Tap-grind farm game whose free path deliberately gets 'steeper' (tap requirements escalate 1,2,4) and a $4.99 paid skip appears, manufacturing friction to sell skips.
Settings with Delete account one click inside; account destruction easy and reachable, no buried opt-out.
Fake scarcity: 'Only 3 left!' changes to 5, then 1, then 4 across reloads with zero purchases — the stock counter is fabricated.
Cookie banner with both Accept all and Reject all equally styled and visible; symmetric choice, no dark pattern.
Checkout shows subtotal $89, free shipping, total $89 with guest checkout option; no hidden fees or forced account.
Data export button ('no strings attached') and invite-friends section explicitly marked optional with 'no feature depends on this number'; honest.
Gamified referral escalation ('just 2 invites from VIP Legend', hyperbolic tier promises) engineered to pressure users into recruiting contacts.
Hotel booking shows $19/night and full total $70.75 including all fees (service, booking, convenience) above the fold before checkout; fully transparent.
Newsletter unsubscribe one click with confirmation and clear 'Yes, unsubscribe'; easy opt-out, no retention tricks.
Level gated behind forced unskippable ad ('verified attention time is the only accepted currency') that pauses and resets progress if you look away — attention-hijacking monetization.
Consent banner with huge bold Accept All and tiny faded 'Manage options'/'Essential cookies only' alternatives; asymmetric choice architecture favoring consent.
Ad embedded in article reading flow labeled 'Continue reading' with prominent Next CTA inside the ad block, masquerading as a reading control; ad bait.
Blocking cookie overlay with no dismissal (Esc/backdrop do nothing, 'By continuing you agree') — forced action with no neutral exit; only compliance paths.
Clearly labeled 'Sponsored' video ad with visible Skip ad button; honest advertising.
Invite dialog sends a welcome offer to user-selected contacts 'as your personal invite'; disclosed but uses personal-invite framing that may exploit recipient trust.

Checked Immortal Accounts (deletion is 1 click, equal visual weight to Keep), Forced Grace Period (no delayed execution; 'access ends at end of billing period' is factual, not a delay), Cuteness (no affective assets injected in cancel flow) — no pattern triggers.
Drip Pricing #1: P(s0)=$96.12 equals P(sn), no sequential inflation across states; #3: fee terms (Tax) present in the initial order summary, nothing concealed until checkout.

Addictive Design #3: reinforcement lexemes ('streak', 'level up', 'claim reward', 'daily bonus', 'spin again') at high density; FOMO #3 'resets soon / don't lose your streak'; Limited Time Message #3: 'resets soon' has zero temporal specificity while maximizing urgency; variable-ratio reward admitted ('35% nothing, 10% jackpot').

Privacy Zuckering #1: essential ToS and monetization are SEPARATE checkboxes, data-sharing explicitly 'Optional', no bundled consent; Bad Defaults: no checkbox pre-checked; Automatic Accept Third Party Term: no pre-checked legal box.

Pay-To-Play #1: free effort escalates exponentially (1, 2, 4 taps per stage, c=2) while paid bypass is O(1) ('Skip this stage instantly — $4.99', 'Paid bypass: 1 tap'); Grinding #1: effort scales c^i while stage value only increments linearly — manufactured friction monetized.

Immortal Accounts #1/#2/#3: deletion affordance present, one click from Settings (depth 1-2), no missing deletion vector, no visual demotion; Labyrinthine Navigation: depth << threshold. No pattern triggers.

Low Stock #3: stock quantifier inconsistent across loads within seconds ('Only 3 left' -> '5' -> '1' -> '4') with 0 transactions in log — fabricated inventory; FOMO #1/#2: pulsing urgency badge ('animate-pulse') with no genuine scarcity.

Privacy Maze #1: d(start,accept)=1 = d(start,reject)=1, no path asymmetry; #2: Accept and Reject rendered with identical classes (same border/accent/bg), no prominence disparity; no confirmshaming or hidden options.
Forced Registration #1: guest checkout path exists ('Checkout as guest'), no absolute state blocking; Drip Pricing: subtotal/shipping/total all disclosed at s0; no hidden fees.

Address Book Leeching #3: invite section explicitly framed 'optional' with 'No feature depends on this number' — no benefactive reframing of a permission; no blocked functionality; data export honest.

Social Pyramid #3: referral-reward language escalates hyperbolically across tiers ('stickers' -> 'inner circle of top creators' -> 'ultimate power & limitless glory!!!') — intensity growth exceeds linear; #1: progression gated on invite counts (1/3/10); FOMO #3: 'just 2 invites from VIP Legend' urgency claim.

Drip Pricing #3: mandatory-fee terms (reservation service fee, booking fee, convenience charge) present in the INITIAL state s0 above the fold with full total $70.75; #1: P(s0)=P(sn), no price inflation across states.

Offboarding check: unsubscribe is 1 click with confirmation; Forced Continuity #3: no guilt language gap (no 'lose your benefits' framing, just 'Keep subscription' vs 'Yes, unsubscribe'); no grace-period or reversal trap.

Watch Ads To Unlock #1: reward (1 Energy) gated on uninterrupted ad playback — 'verified attention time is the only accepted currency'; Countdown On Ads #1: Skip button disabled (disabled attr, line-through) until ad completes — temporal gating of navigational agency; #3: ad framed as 'earn' exchange.

Privacy Maze #2 / False Hierarchy #2: Accept All is a large bold filled button (py-3, text-12px, font-bold, shadow-lg) while alternatives are tiny faded text ('Manage options' 9px 40% opacity, 'Essential cookies only' 8px 30% opacity); Customisation #1: accept path = 1 click, reject path requires nested 'Manage options' (d>=2).

Disguised Ad #3: ad container labeled 'Continue reading' with a prominent 'Next' CTA inside the ad block — semantic mimicry of native reading-flow action labels; Feedforward Ambiguity: ad Next button reads as article continuation but resolves to the ad; native pagination is a separate, smaller control.

Dead End #1/#2: overlay with z-index 120 (>100) and zero dismissal vectors — 'Esc pressed? Backdrop clicked? Nothing happens — those edges simply don't exist'; every path forces a compliance decision, no neutral exit ('You never got a neutral exit'); Automatic Accept #3: 'By continuing you agree' consent-by-continuation language.

Countdown On Ads #1/#2: skip affordance is PRESENT and enabled from the start (Skip ad button, not disabled), ad labeled 'Sponsored' — no temporal gating of dismissal, no dynamic affordance injection; standard skippable preroll ad.

Friend Spam #3 Sender Identity Spoofing: message sent 'as your personal invite' — the system injects the user's identity into the sender alias of a corporate marketing message (SenderAlias=I_user, Author=I_corp), using the user as a trojan horse to their contacts; granular selection exists but identity spoofing triggers.
